findings.title: Scope sanity check 'Are explicit exclusions documented?' (B0041) never fails: an empty Out of scope on a saved charter gives 'unknown', and a whitespace-only Out of scope gives 'pass'
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone at eb8163e2 (candidate 089a2a2f…), fresh PostgreSQL 16 and API (AUTH_MODE=dev, synthetic seed), Node 24.21.0: `with-stack.sh node live-scenario.mjs`. As dev.lead: POST /api/v1/transformations (end_to_end), then POST /transformations/{id}/charter with name, sponsor, lead, case for change, in scope and baseline date but no outOfScope. GET /charter returns scopeCheckPrechecks[exclusions_documented] = {result:'unknown', detail:'No exclusions (out of scope) are recorded yet.'}. Then PATCH /charter {outOfScope:'   '} returns 200, stores '   ', and the same pre-check returns 'pass' ('Explicit exclusions are documented.'). The charter screen renders the 'unknown' state as a grey 'Unknown' badge and the whitespace case as green 'Supported by data'. Source: apps/api/src/modules/transformations/charter.ts:250-253 (`c.out_of_scope === null ? unknown : pass`), and packages/shared/src/schemas/charter.ts `outOfScope: text(1, 20000)` (min length counts whitespace). The result enum has 'attention' but this pre-check never uses it.
findings.expected: Register acceptance for REQ-PB-031: 'an empty Out of scope field makes 'Are explicit exclusions documented?' fail'. On a saved charter the Out of scope field is known to be empty (charter field B0035 'Out of scope: [Explicit exclusions]'), so the B0041 check fails, for example with the 'attention' result and a reason. A blank or whitespace-only value is not a documented exclusion and must not pass.
findings.actual: Empty Out of scope gives 'unknown' (neutral grey, not a failure), and whitespace-only gives 'pass' (green). The check can therefore never fail, and the assigned acceptance criterion is not met. ADR-0017 §2 ('missing data gives unknown') is applied to a field whose emptiness is itself the B0041 answer.

history.note: raised by domain-reviewer DG2 round 2 re-run (T-DG2-REV-DOM-R2B); independently reproduced on the live stack. Medium; mandatory because the assigned REQ-PB-031 acceptance criterion is unmet.

findings.title: Product-gate list cards and detail headings repeat the gate code ('G2 – G2 - Direction') in English and Arabic
findings.reproduction: Live P2 Playwright journey (apps/web/e2e/p2-journeys.spec.ts, chromium-en and chromium-ar) on the disposable stack: open Gates and Gate G2. Cards read 'G1 – G1 - Case for Change', 'G2 – G2 - Direction', … 'G6 – G6 - Sustain'. The detail heading reads 'G2 – G2 - Direction'. In Arabic it reads 'G2 – G2 - التوجّه'. Cause: apps/web/src/pages/gates/GatesPage.tsx:70 and GateDetailPage.tsx:74 prefix `${code} – ` to sourceNameEn/nameAr, which the seed (0011_p2_methodology_catalogue.sql) already stores as the B0023 gate column 'G2 - Direction'. The API values are correct and verbatim.
findings.expected: The gate title shows the B0023 name once, for example 'G2 - Direction' (or the code plus the name without the code prefix), in both languages.
findings.actual: The code is shown twice in every gate title on the list and detail screens (EN and AR). This is a cosmetic fidelity defect; the gate logic is unaffected.

history.note: raised by domain-reviewer DG2 round 2 re-run (T-DG2-REV-DOM-R2B); independently reproduced in EN and AR screenshots. Low, non-mandatory.

findings.title: Register names a per-dimension endpoint that does not exist (GET /api/v1/transformations/{id}/tom/dimensions/{dim}); the view is served by GET /tom-canvas
findings.reproduction: requirements.csv REQ-S05-003 screen_api = 'Target Operating Model > Dimension; GET /api/v1/transformations/{id}/tom/dimensions/{dim}'. On the live stack, GET /api/v1/transformations/{id}/tom/dimensions/customer_value_proposition returns 404, and docs/api/openapi.yaml has no such path. The behaviour itself exists: GET /transformations/{id}/tom-canvas returns 10 cells, each with cell (current/target design, owner), dimension, gaps, decisions, dependencies and evidence, and the Design page renders the DimensionView (live-canvas.log).
findings.expected: The register's screen/API column names the real contract (GET …/tom-canvas, plus the per-dimension view in the Design page), so the register stays an honest map to the implementation.
findings.actual: The register cites a non-existent endpoint for an IMPLEMENTED requirement. Documentation drift only; no behaviour gap.
